l: relation extraction, HYBGRAG: Hybrid Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Textual and Relational Knowledge Bases, appendix .. C.1.2
s: Relation extraction is refined through corrective feedback when relations used for retrieval are judged incorrect. In one example, the relations associated with disease and expression were removed, leaving a protein-protein interaction relation.

l: corrective feedback, HYBGRAG: Hybrid Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Textual and Relational Knowledge Bases, appendix .. C.1.2
s: Corrective feedback is provided when retrieval or evaluation is incorrect, indicating that the retrieval input, extracted entity, relation, domain, or selected module may be wrong. HYBGRAG uses this feedback to revise its retrieval decisions.

l: CRAG, HYBGRAG: Hybrid Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Textual and Relational Knowledge Bases, appendix .. C.1.2
s: CRAG does not provide ground truth for retrieval, so corrective feedback is constructed from the router's action and the evaluation. The unit explains that incorrect graph retrieval may reflect faulty inputs or domain selection, while incorrect text retrieval indicates that the current document batch was not useful.

l: HYBGRAG: Hybrid Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Textual and Relational Knowledge Bases, HYBGRAG: Hybrid Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Textual and Relational Knowledge Bases, notes
s: This unit consists of a link to an Anthropic webpage. The webpage is titled or associated with the Claude 3 family. No further information about the Claude 3 family is provided in the unit.

l: Claude 3 family, HYBGRAG: Hybrid Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Textual and Relational Knowledge Bases, notes
s: The Claude 3 family is referenced through a link to an Anthropic webpage, but the unit provides no further information about it.

l: HYBGRAG: Hybrid Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Textual and Relational Knowledge Bases, HYBGRAG: Hybrid Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Textual and Relational Knowledge Bases, appendix
s: The unit evaluates design choices in HYBGRAG for CRAG and reports that using context and in-context learning improves accuracy and reduces hallucination compared with no context, while oracle settings perform best. It describes HYBGRAG's critic module, which identifies errors in question analysis and retrieval-module selection. The unit also specifies CRAG implementation details, including Claude 3 Sonnet as the evaluator, chain-of-thought prompting, and BAAI/bge-m3 for dense retrieval and ranking. It compares ReAct and Corrective RAG with HYBGRAG, noting their different critic designs and retrieval processes.

l: HYBGRAG, HYBGRAG: Hybrid Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Textual and Relational Knowledge Bases, appendix
s: HYBGRAG is evaluated in CRAG through ablations of its validator and commentor settings. Using context and in-context learning improves its accuracy and reduces hallucination relative to using no context, while oracle settings achieve the strongest reported results. Its critic module provides feedback on incorrect question type, dynamism, domain, entity and relation extraction, and retrieval-module selection.

l: CRAG, HYBGRAG: Hybrid Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Textual and Relational Knowledge Bases, appendix
s: CRAG uses Claude 3 Sonnet as its LLM evaluator and chain-of-thought prompting for all generator LLMs. Its dense retrieval and ranking use BAAI/bge-m3, and its implementations of ReAct and Corrective RAG share HYBGRAG's backbone while using different critics.

l: graph retrieval module, HYBGRAG: Hybrid Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Textual and Relational Knowledge Bases, appendix
s: The knowledge graph is one of the reference sources available to HYBGRAG and ReAct. HYBGRAG's critic can select it when the retrieved text does not contain useful information, based on newly extracted entities and relations.

l: Think-on-Graph, HYBGRAG: Hybrid Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Textual and Relational Knowledge Bases, appendix
s: Think-on-Graph is implemented with its provided code using Claude 3 Sonnet as the base model. Because a full experiment takes more than a week, it is evaluated on only 10% of the testing data.

l: Claude 3 Sonnet, HYBGRAG: Hybrid Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Textual and Relational Knowledge Bases, appendix
s: Claude 3 Sonnet serves as the base model for the Think-on-Graph implementation and as the LLM evaluator for CRAG.

l: BAAI/bge-m3, HYBGRAG: Hybrid Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Textual and Relational Knowledge Bases, appendix
s: BAAI/bge-m3 is used as the embedding model for dense retrieval and ranking in CRAG.

l: ReAct, HYBGRAG: Hybrid Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Textual and Relational Knowledge Bases, appendix
s: ReAct shares HYBGRAG's backbone but uses a different critic. It has three actions, search web, search KG, and extract entity relation domain, and iterates among action, observation, and thought for four iterations.

l: Corrective RAG, HYBGRAG: Hybrid Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Textual and Relational Knowledge Bases, appendix
s: Corrective RAG shares HYBGRAG's backbone but uses a different critic. Its implementation uses a pre-trained LLM rather than a fine-tuned retrieval evaluator; it begins with text retrieval, validates whether the reference is correct, ambiguous, or incorrect, and uses graph retrieval when the reference is incorrect before generating a chain-of-thought answer.

l: HYBGRAG: Hybrid Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Textual and Relational Knowledge Bases, HYBGRAG: Hybrid Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Textual and Relational Knowledge Bases, notes
s: The unit consists of the number 6 followed by a GitHub URL. The URL points to the repository associated with ToG. No further information about the repository or ToG is provided.

l: ToG, HYBGRAG: Hybrid Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Textual and Relational Knowledge Bases, notes
s: ToG is associated with the GitHub repository at https://github.com/GasolSun36/ToG. The unit provides no further information about it.

l: HYBGRAG: Hybrid Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Textual and Relational Knowledge Bases, HYBGRAG: Hybrid Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Textual and Relational Knowledge Bases, C.2
s: This unit describes the prompts and workflow components of STARK, CRAG, and HYBGRAG for extracting entities and relations, selecting references, validating answers, and generating responses. STARK uses routers, a validator, and a commentor to decide between the knowledge graph and text documents and to correct extracted information. CRAG classifies each question by type, dynamism, domain, and reference source, then uses reflection, validation, commenting, and generation prompts. The unit also lists entity and relation types for finance, sports, music, movie, and encyclopedia domains, along with HYBGRAG's API-call and token counts.

l: STARK, HYBGRAG: Hybrid Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Textual and Relational Knowledge Bases, C.2
s: STARK uses prompts for first-decision routing, reflection, validation, and commenting. Its workflow extracts topic entities and useful relations, determines whether the knowledge graph or text documents can narrow the search, and revises decisions when retrieved documents are incorrect.

l: CRAG, HYBGRAG: Hybrid Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Textual and Relational Knowledge Bases, C.2
s: CRAG classifies questions by question type, dynamism, and domain, extracts topic entities and useful relations, and selects either the knowledge graph or text documents as a reference source. Its workflow includes router reflection, validation, commenting, generation, and evaluation against a ground-truth answer.

l: HYBGRAG, HYBGRAG: Hybrid Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Textual and Relational Knowledge Bases, C.2
s: HYBGRAG is associated with a table reporting API calls and token counts for its components. The table lists calls and prompt or example tokens for the router, validator, commentor, and generator.

l: router, HYBGRAG: Hybrid Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Textual and Relational Knowledge Bases, C.2
s: The router extracts entities and relations, chooses between the knowledge graph and text documents, and classifies CRAG questions by type, dynamism, and domain. Its reflection prompts ask it to reconsider incorrect predictions or references.

l: validator, HYBGRAG: Hybrid Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Textual and Relational Knowledge Bases, C.2
s: The validator determines whether a retrieved document is aligned with the question in STARK and whether a generated prediction answers the question in CRAG. It responds with yes or no.

l: commentor, HYBGRAG: Hybrid Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Textual and Relational Knowledge Bases, C.2
s: The commentor identifies wrong entities or relations in STARK and incorrect reference sources, question types, dynamism, or domains in CRAG.

l: generator LLMs, HYBGRAG: Hybrid Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Textual and Relational Knowledge Bases, C.2
s: The generator produces a final answer from a question, references, reference source, query time, question type, dynamism, and domain. Its prompt instructs it to identify and solve all necessary subproblems and to answer invalid question when a false premise or assumption is present.

l: knowledge graph, HYBGRAG: Hybrid Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Textual and Relational Knowledge Bases, C.2
s: The knowledge graph is presented as a possible reference for narrowing the search space and answering questions. Each entity in the knowledge graph is associated with a document.

l: text documents, HYBGRAG: Hybrid Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Textual and Relational Knowledge Bases, C.2
s: Text documents are presented as a possible source for answering questions and narrowing the search space. The STARK prompts require documents to answer the given question and allow a later batch of text documents when a reference is not useful.

l: topic entities, HYBGRAG: Hybrid Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Textual and Relational Knowledge Bases, C.2
s: An entity must have exactly one category in parentheses in the extraction prompts. The listed domains define entity types such as company_name, nba_team_name, artist, actor, and encyclopedia_entity.

l: useful relations, HYBGRAG: Hybrid Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Textual and Relational Knowledge Bases, C.2
s: Relations must come from the provided relational types. The unit lists domain-specific relations for finance, sports, music, movie, and encyclopedia questions.

l: question, HYBGRAG: Hybrid Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Textual and Relational Knowledge Bases, C.2
s: A question is supplied to the routing, extraction, validation, commenting, and generation prompts. It may be classified by type, dynamism, and domain and may require a knowledge graph or text documents for an answer.

l: question type, HYBGRAG: Hybrid Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Textual and Relational Knowledge Bases, C.2
s: CRAG classifies a question as simple, simple_w_condition, set, comparison, aggregation, multi_hop, post_processing, or false_premise.

l: question dynamism, HYBGRAG: Hybrid Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Textual and Relational Knowledge Bases, C.2
s: CRAG classifies the dynamism of a question as real-time, fast-changing, slow-changing, or static.

l: question domain, HYBGRAG: Hybrid Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Textual and Relational Knowledge Bases, C.2
s: CRAG classifies a question into one of five domains: music, movie, finance, sports, or encyclopedia.

l: reference source, HYBGRAG: Hybrid Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Textual and Relational Knowledge Bases, C.2
s: The reference source is selected as either the knowledge graph or text documents. CRAG's prompts require the system to choose the source most useful for answering the question.

l: VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, Abstract
s: The text introduces VideoRAG, a framework that dynamically retrieves videos relevant to queries and uses their visual and textual information for response generation. It addresses limitations in existing Retrieval-Augmented Generation approaches, which mainly focus on text, sometimes images, and often overlook videos or reduce them to textual descriptions. VideoRAG is powered by Large Video Language Models, which represent videos for retrieval and integrate retrieved videos with queries. The framework also includes a video frame selection mechanism and a strategy for extracting textual information when subtitles are unavailable, and experiments show that it outperforms relevant baselines.

l: Retrieval-Augmented Generation, VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, Abstract
s: Retrieval-Augmented Generation improves factual accuracy by retrieving external knowledge relevant to queries and incorporating it into generation. Existing approaches primarily focus on text, with some considering images, while largely overlooking videos.

l: VideoRAG, VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, Abstract
s: VideoRAG dynamically retrieves videos based on their relevance to queries and uses both visual and textual information for response generation. It includes a video frame selection mechanism and a strategy for extracting textual information from videos without subtitles. Experiments show that VideoRAG is superior to relevant baselines.

l: Large Video Language Models, VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, Abstract
s: Large Video Language Models power VideoRAG by directly processing video content for retrieval representation and integrating retrieved videos jointly with queries during response generation.

l: videos, VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, Abstract
s: Videos are presented as a rich source of multimodal knowledge that can represent contextual details more effectively than other modalities. VideoRAG retrieves them dynamically and uses their visual and textual information, while addressing the difficulty of processing all frames in extremely long videos.

l: multimodal knowledge, VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, Abstract
s: Multimodal knowledge is described as a strength of videos because it can represent contextual details more effectively than any other modality.

l: queries, VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, Abstract
s: Queries are used by VideoRAG to determine which videos are relevant for retrieval. Retrieved videos are integrated jointly with queries for response generation.

l: generation, VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, Abstract
s: Responses are generated using retrieved videos together with queries, incorporating both visual and textual information through VideoRAG.

l: adaptive frame selection, VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, Abstract
s: The video frame selection mechanism extracts the most informative subset of frames from videos. It is introduced because Large Video Language Models may not have sufficient context size for all frames in extremely long videos and because some frames are more important than others.

l: VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, Introduction
s: The unit introduces VideoRAG, a framework that retrieves relevant videos and incorporates their visual and textual content into answers to user queries. It addresses limitations of text- and image-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation by using videos to represent temporal dynamics, spatial details, and multimodal cues. VideoRAG uses a frame selection model to reduce long-video redundancy and automatic speech recognition to generate transcripts when textual descriptions are unavailable. Its evaluation uses queries from WikiHowQA and query-video pairs from HowTo100M, with results showing improvements over relevant baselines.

l: VideoRAG, VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, Introduction
s: VideoRAG retrieves relevant videos from a large video corpus and integrates visual and textual elements into answer generation. It uses a frame selection model and automatically generated transcripts to make video retrieval and processing more effective.

l: Retrieval-Augmented Generation, VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, Introduction
s: Retrieval-Augmented Generation retrieves query-relevant information from external knowledge sources and incorporates that information when generating answers. Existing approaches have primarily focused on textual content, with more recent work extending retrieval to images or text-image pairs.

l: large foundation models, VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, Introduction
s: Large foundation models, including large language models and their extensions to vision, have become standard for diverse tasks because of their capabilities. Despite encoding extensive knowledge in their parameters, they can generate factually incorrect outputs because their knowledge may be inaccurate or outdated.

l: large vision-language models, VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, Introduction
s: Large vision-language models are described as extensions of large language models to the vision modality. They are trained on extensive textual and multimodal corpora and are used for diverse tasks.

l: Large Video Language Models, VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, Introduction
s: Large Video Language Models are used by VideoRAG to process video content containing visual and textual information within a unified framework. Their capabilities help the framework capture the multimodal richness of videos during answer generation.

l: videos, VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, Introduction
s: Videos are presented as an underutilized external knowledge source for RAG systems. They combine temporal dynamics, spatial details, and multimodal cues, enabling them to represent complex processes, context-dependent interactions, and non-verbal signals that static modalities may miss.

l: video corpus, VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, Introduction
s: The video corpus serves as the large collection from which VideoRAG retrieves videos relevant to user queries.

l: visual and textual modalities, VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, Introduction
s: The visual and textual modalities are jointly used to represent videos and support their retrieval. VideoRAG obtains textual information through transcripts when descriptions such as subtitles are unavailable.

l: adaptive frame selection, VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, Introduction
s: The frame selection model is introduced to extract the most informative subset of frames from long and redundant videos. It is trained to maximize retrieval and generation performance while reducing the amount of video content processed by Large Video Language Models.

l: automatic speech recognition, VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, Introduction
s: Automatic speech recognition is used to generate textual transcripts from videos when textual descriptions are unavailable. These transcripts allow VideoRAG to use both visual and textual information for every video.

l: WikiHowQA, VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, Introduction
s: WikiHowQA provides overlapping queries and query-answer pairs used to evaluate VideoRAG.

l: HowTo100M, VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, Introduction
s: HowTo100M provides query-video pairs without answers for the evaluation of VideoRAG. The datasets are used to automatically collect a dataset for RAG over videos.

l: VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, Method .. 2.4 / Auxiliary Text Generation
s: The unit introduces VideoRAG, a retrieval-augmented generation framework that uses a video corpus as its external knowledge source. It retrieves query-relevant videos, selects informative frames, and generates responses grounded in the retrieved visual and textual information. The unit also describes large video language models, adaptive frame selection, frame space reduction with clustering, and auxiliary text generation from audio when subtitles are unavailable.

l: VideoRAG, VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, Method .. 2.4 / Auxiliary Text Generation
s: VideoRAG extends retrieval-augmented generation by retrieving relevant videos from a video corpus and using them to generate grounded responses. It combines video retrieval, frame selection, and video-augmented response generation.

l: Retrieval-Augmented Generation, VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, Method .. 2.4 / Auxiliary Text Generation
s: Retrieval-augmented generation retrieves relevant knowledge elements from an external corpus and supplies them to a foundation model to produce an answer. In this unit, the external knowledge source is extended from mainly text and static images to videos.

l: Large Video Language Models, VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, Method .. 2.4 / Auxiliary Text Generation
s: Large video language models process visual frames and associated textual data together. Their vision and text encoders produce visual and textual representations that can be jointly processed to represent videos and generate responses.

l: video corpus, VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, Method .. 2.4 / Auxiliary Text Generation
s: The video corpus serves as the external knowledge source for VideoRAG. Videos in the corpus are compared with a query so that the most relevant ones can be retrieved.

l: video retrieval, VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, Method .. 2.4 / Auxiliary Text Generation
s: Video retrieval identifies query-relevant videos from the video corpus. It obtains representations for the query and each video with a large video language model, compares them using representation-level similarity such as cosine similarity, and selects the top-k videos.

l: generation, VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, Method .. 2.4 / Auxiliary Text Generation
s: Response generation concatenates frames and associated textual data from retrieved videos, combines the resulting multimodal inputs with the query, and forwards them to a large video language model. The model generates a response grounded in the retrieved videos.

l: adaptive frame selection, VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, Method .. 2.4 / Auxiliary Text Generation
s: Adaptive frame selection extracts an informative and computationally feasible subset of frames instead of processing every frame or uniformly sampling them. It selects the subset with the highest score, using query-guided selection during generation.

l: frame space reduction with clustering, VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, Method .. 2.4 / Auxiliary Text Generation
s: Frame space reduction with clustering uses k-means++ to divide all video frames into groups and selects the frame closest to each cluster centroid. Frame selection then operates on this reduced representative set, substantially reducing the search space while preserving frame diversity.

l: auxiliary text generation, VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, Method .. 2.4 / Auxiliary Text Generation
s: Auxiliary text generation supplies textual data for videos that lack subtitles. It extracts audio from a video and converts the audio into text using off-the-shelf automatic speech recognition techniques.

l: videos, VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, Method .. 2.4 / Auxiliary Text Generation
s: A video is represented as a sequence of visual frames and may include associated textual data such as subtitles. In VideoRAG, videos are retrieved, their frames are selected, and their visual and textual information is provided to a large video language model.

l: frames, VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, Method .. 2.4 / Auxiliary Text Generation
s: Frames provide the visual content used for video representation, retrieval, and response generation. Because videos may contain many redundant or irrelevant frames, VideoRAG selects informative frames and can use cluster representatives to reduce processing requirements.

l: queries, VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, Method .. 2.4 / Auxiliary Text Generation
s: The query is represented as textual information and is compared with video representations during retrieval. During response generation, it is appended to the selected multimodal content to guide the generated response.

l: VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, opening .. Case Study
s: This unit reports experiments evaluating VideoRAG for question answering with WikiHowQA and HowTo100M, including human-written and automatically generated query-answer pairs. VideoRAG, especially VIDEORAG-V and VIDEORAG-VT, outperforms textual, text-image, and text-video RAG baselines across most reported metrics, while oracle retrieval indicates further gains are possible from better video retrieval. The experiments find that combining textual and visual features improves retrieval, adaptive frame selection improves both retrieval and generation, and larger LVLMs generally improve performance. Human evaluation also favors VIDEORAG-VT, and a case study shows that retrieved video enables a detailed answer about baking cookies on a car dashboard.

l: VideoRAG, VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, opening .. Case Study
s: VideoRAG is evaluated as a video-based retrieval-augmented generation approach for question answering. Its variants outperform conventional textual, text-image, and text-video RAG baselines, and its performance improves with better video retrieval, adaptive frame selection, and larger LVLMs.

l: VIDEORAG-V, VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, opening .. Case Study
s: VIDEORAG-V uses video frames exclusively as generation context to provide visual grounding. It generally outperforms the RAG baselines and achieves strong results on both WikiHowQA and synthetic QA with HowTo100M.

l: VIDEORAG-VT, VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, opening .. Case Study
s: VIDEORAG-VT jointly uses video frames and textual transcripts. It achieves strong performance across the experiments and receives the highest human-evaluation score among the compared methods.

l: WikiHowQA, VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, opening .. Case Study
s: WikiHowQA provides instructional questions extracted from WikiHow webpages with human-written ground truths. It is used to evaluate VideoRAG and the comparison systems.

l: HowTo100M, VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, opening .. Case Study
s: HowTo100M supplies instruction videos from YouTube and is associated with WikiHow queries through search results. It is also used to generate synthetic query-answer pairs for evaluation.

l: NAÏVE, VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, opening .. Case Study
s: NAÏVE generates answers from queries without additional context. It performs below the RAG methods and, in the car-dashboard cookie case study, gives a generic refusal rather than the requested procedure.

l: TEXTRAG (BM25), VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, opening .. Case Study
s: TEXTRAG (BM25) retrieves Wikipedia documents using BM25 and generates answers grounded in them. It improves over NAÏVE but generally performs below the multimodal and video-based approaches.

l: TEXTRAG (DPR), VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, opening .. Case Study
s: TEXTRAG (DPR) retrieves textual documents using DPR before generation. It improves over NAÏVE in many results but is generally outperformed by VideoRAG.

l: TEXTIMAGERAG, VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, opening .. Case Study
s: TEXTIMAGERAG retrieves a query-relevant textual document and image for generation. It outperforms the basic text-only baselines but generally trails the video-based approaches.

l: TEXTVIDEORAG, VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, opening .. Case Study
s: TEXTVIDEORAG represents videos as textual descriptions such as captions or transcripts and uses only that textual information for retrieval and generation. It is generally weaker than VIDEORAG-V and VIDEORAG-VT.

l: LLaVA-Video, VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, opening .. Case Study
s: LLaVA-Video is used as a 7B-parameter LVLM for answer generation. VideoRAG variants evaluated with it outperform the listed non-video baselines.

l: InternVL2.5, VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, opening .. Case Study
s: InternVL2.5 is used for generation at 8B parameters and in experiments with varying model sizes. Its VideoRAG performance improves as the model size increases.

l: Qwen2.5-VL, VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, opening .. Case Study
s: Qwen2.5-VL is used as a 3B-parameter LVLM for generation. Its results also show benefits from video-based context, particularly when video frames and transcripts are combined.

l: ROUGE-L, VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, opening .. Case Study
s: ROUGE-L measures the longest common subsequence between generated answers and ground truths. It is one of the four metrics used to compare the systems.

l: BLEU-4, VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, opening .. Case Study
s: BLEU-4 measures n-gram overlap up to four grams between generated and reference answers. It is reported alongside ROUGE-L, BERTScore, and G-Eval.

l: BERTScore, VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, opening .. Case Study
s: BERTScore measures semantic alignment by comparing BERT-derived embeddings of generated and reference answers. It is used as an automatic evaluation metric.

l: G-Eval, VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, opening .. Case Study
s: G-Eval uses GPT-4o-mini to rate generated answers against references on a five-point Likert scale. Its scores broadly track human evaluation, with a reported human-model agreement coefficient of 0.588.

l: Retrieval-Augmented Generation, VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, opening .. Case Study
s: RAG systems outperform the NAÏVE baseline, supporting the value of external knowledge for factual answer generation. The results indicate that video content can provide richer information than textual, text-image, or text-description-based alternatives.

l: video retrieval, VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, opening .. Case Study
s: Video retrieval is identified as a critical factor in RAG performance. Oracle retrieval produces the strongest results, indicating room for improvement in retrieval mechanisms.

l: visual features, VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, opening .. Case Study
s: Visual features alone underperform textual features for retrieval, likely because textual queries align more strongly with text-based representations. They remain complementary to textual features, and combining both improves retrieval.

l: textual features, VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, opening .. Case Study
s: Textual features consistently outperform visual features for video retrieval because of their stronger semantic alignment with textual queries. An ensemble of textual and visual features achieves the best retrieval results, with a slight emphasis on textual features generally preferred.

l: question answering, VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, opening .. Case Study
s: Question answering is the task used to evaluate VideoRAG and the baselines. The evaluation covers WikiHowQA questions and synthetic questions associated with HowTo100M.

l: human evaluation, VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, opening .. Case Study
s: Human evaluation uses 12 evaluators to assess responses to 50 randomly sampled queries on a five-point Likert scale. VIDEORAG-VT receives the highest score, and the reported inter-annotator Spearman correlation is 0.632.

l: video frames, VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, opening .. Case Study
s: Video frames provide visual context for VideoRAG generation and are also used in visual retrieval features. The experiments use four frames per video for retrieval and up to 32 frames for generation, with adaptive selection outperforming uniform sampling.

l: textual transcripts, VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, opening .. Case Study
s: Textual transcripts can be jointly used with video frames in VIDEORAG-VT. The experiments show that transcripts provide useful complementary information, although visual features alone capture much of the information needed for generation.

l: car dashboard, VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, opening .. Case Study
s: The car dashboard appears in a case study asking how to bake cookies on it. A retrieved video enables VIDEORAG-V to provide steps involving a sunny spot, cookie dough, a baking sheet, and a dashboard temperature of at least 95 degrees Fahrenheit.

l: cookies, VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, opening .. Case Study
s: Cookies are the subject of the case study comparing NAÏVE with VIDEORAG-V. The retrieved-video answer describes placing cookie dough on a prepared baking sheet and leaving it on a sunny car dashboard until the edges are firm.

l: VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, 4 / Retrieval-Augmented Generation .. Large Video Language Models
s: This unit explains Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) as a process that retrieves relevant documents and uses them to generate grounded answers. It describes Multimodal RAG efforts involving images, code, tables, and audio, while emphasizing that videos provide temporal, spatial, and multimodal information. The unit introduces VideoRAG, which dynamically retrieves and holistically uses video content to address limitations of existing video-based RAG approaches. It also discusses Large Video Language Models (LVLMs), whose video-understanding capabilities enable VideoRAG.

l: Retrieval-Augmented Generation, VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Video Corpus, 4 / Retrieval-Augmented Generation .. Large Video Language Models
s: Retrieval-Augmented Generation combines retrieval and generation to produce answers grounded in external knowledge. Most RAG research has focused on text, leaving comparatively little effort devoted to incorporating images and other modalities.

l: Stage-I training, SimRAG: Self-Improving Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Adapting Large Language Models to Specialized Domains, Related Work
s: Retrieval-oriented fine-tuning is the first stage of SimRAG. It includes fine-tuning on general supervised fine-tuning data, general domain question-answering data, and retrieval-related data.

s: Domain adaptive fine-tuning with self-training is the second stage of SimRAG. In this stage, the model extracts candidate answers from the corpus, generates candidate questions conditioned on documents and answers, and is further fine-tuned on the filtered pseudo-labeled examples.

l: round-trip consistency filtering, SimRAG: Self-Improving Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Adapting Large Language Models to Specialized Domains, Related Work
s: Round-trip consistency is used to filter pseudo-labeled tuples generated by SimRAG. The retained tuples contain a question, documents, and an answer.

l: question answering, SimRAG: Self-Improving Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Adapting Large Language Models to Specialized Domains, Related Work
s: Question answering is identified as a knowledge-intensive NLP task supported by retrieval-augmented generation. SimRAG is designed to adapt LLMs to domain-specific question-answering tasks.

l: pseudo-labeled data, SimRAG: Self-Improving Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Adapting Large Language Models to Specialized Domains, Related Work
s: Pseudo-labeled tuples are generated by extracting candidate answers from corpus documents and then generating candidate questions conditioned on the documents and answers. SimRAG filters these tuples with round-trip consistency before using them for further fine-tuning.

l: SimRAG: Self-Improving Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Adapting Large Language Models to Specialized Domains, SimRAG: Self-Improving Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Adapting Large Language Models to Specialized Domains, Methodology / Problem Setup .. Stage-II: Domain Adaptive Fine-tuning
s: This unit describes a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) setup in which a retriever selects relevant contexts and an LLM generates an answer to a query. Stage-I retrieval-oriented fine-tuning trains instruction-tuned LLMs on general instruction, context-aware QA, and retrieval-related data. Stage-II domain adaptive fine-tuning uses self-training on an unlabeled specialized-domain corpus to generate, retrieve, and filter pseudo-labeled QA samples. The resulting samples are blended with general instruction and context-aware QA data to adapt the LLM to specialized domains.

s: The retriever selects the top-k most relevant contexts for a query from a corpus. A strong retriever such as Dragon is also used to filter synthetic QA pairs.

s: The LLM generates answers from queries and retrieved contexts. It is fine-tuned in Stage-I on general retrieval-oriented tasks and then adapted in Stage-II to specialized domains through synthetic data.

s: Stage-I retrieval-oriented fine-tuning trains an instruction-tuned LLM on general instruction, context-aware QA, and retrieval-related data. It targets improved context use, answer generation, and query generation for knowledge-intensive tasks.

l: Stage-II training, SimRAG: Self-Improving Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Adapting Large Language Models to Specialized Domains, Methodology / Problem Setup .. Stage-II: Domain Adaptive Fine-tuning
s: Stage-II domain adaptive fine-tuning adapts the Stage-I model to specialized domains using pseudo-labeled samples generated from unlabeled domain corpora. The synthetic samples are combined with general instruction and context-aware QA data for continued fine-tuning.

l: self-training, SimRAG: Self-Improving Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Adapting Large Language Models to Specialized Domains, Methodology / Problem Setup .. Stage-II: Domain Adaptive Fine-tuning
s: Self-training uses the fine-tuned LLM to generate pseudo-labeled query, context, and answer tuples from specialized-domain text. The generated samples are filtered before being used for further training.

l: specialized domains, SimRAG: Self-Improving Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Adapting Large Language Models to Specialized Domains, Methodology / Problem Setup .. Stage-II: Domain Adaptive Fine-tuning
s: Specialized domains are the target environments for adaptation when labeled data is scarce and distribution shift can reduce performance. Their unlabeled corpora supply documents for synthetic training data generation.

l: unlabeled corpora, SimRAG: Self-Improving Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Adapting Large Language Models to Specialized Domains, Methodology / Problem Setup .. Stage-II: Domain Adaptive Fine-tuning
s: The unlabeled corpus provides specialized-domain documents from which candidate answer spans and questions are generated. These documents also serve as potential supporting contexts during retrieval-based filtering.

l: pseudo-labeled training samples, SimRAG: Self-Improving Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Adapting Large Language Models to Specialized Domains, Methodology / Problem Setup .. Stage-II: Domain Adaptive Fine-tuning
s: Pseudo-labeled training samples consist of generated queries, retrieved or source documents, and generated answers. Samples are retained when the answer appears in the top-k documents retrieved for the generated query.

l: question, SimRAG: Self-Improving Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Adapting Large Language Models to Specialized Domains, Methodology / Problem Setup .. Stage-II: Domain Adaptive Fine-tuning
s: A query is used by the retriever to select relevant contexts, after which the LLM generates an answer. In Stage-II, queries are generated from candidate answers and their source documents.

s: Supporting documents provide the evidence or context used by the LLM to answer a query. In the synthetic-data process, documents from the specialized corpus ground candidate answers and generated questions.

s: A context is a retrieved document or set of documents supplied to the LLM for answer generation. Stage-I includes context-aware QA training, and Stage-II filters samples according to whether the answer occurs in retrieved contexts.

s: An answer is generated by the LLM from a query and its context. In Stage-II, candidate answer spans are first generated from documents and are then used as ground-truth answers for query generation.

l: SimRAG: Self-Improving Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Adapting Large Language Models to Specialized Domains, SimRAG: Self-Improving Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Adapting Large Language Models to Specialized Domains, Experimental Setup / Tasks and Datasets .. Implementation Details
s: The Experimental Setup evaluates SimRAG and multiple baselines across medical, scientific, and computer science datasets, using task-specific metrics and retrieval-augmented inference. The medical evaluation includes the five datasets in the MIRAGE benchmark plus LiveQA and MedicationQA, while the scientific evaluation includes MMLU scientific subsets, ARC-challenge, and SciQ, and the computer science evaluation uses CS-Bench. The study compares general, domain-specific, and retrieval-augmented language models, including GPT-3.5, GPT-4, Llama3-8B-Instruct, Gemma2-27B-Instruct, RAFT, EvidenceRAG, and SimRAG. SimRAG achieves strong results in the medical and scientific tables, and removing Stage-II training lowers its average performance.

l: medical domain, SimRAG: Self-Improving Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Adapting Large Language Models to Specialized Domains, Experimental Setup / Tasks and Datasets .. Implementation Details

s: Stage-I training uses a learning rate of 5e-7, a global batch size of 64, gradient accumulation of 8, and one training epoch. AdamW is used with β1=0.9 and β2=0.95.

l: SimRAG: Self-Improving Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Adapting Large Language Models to Specialized Domains, SimRAG: Self-Improving Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Adapting Large Language Models to Specialized Domains, Experimental Results / Main Results .. Case Studies
s: This unit evaluates SimRAG, an instruction fine-tuning framework for retrieval-augmented, domain-specific question answering across medical, scientific, and computer science domains. SimRAG consistently outperforms baseline models across multiple question-answering formats and approaches GPT-4 performance when using Gemma2-27B as its backbone. Ablation studies show that retrieval-oriented fine-tuning in Stage-I and self-synthesized training tuples in Stage-II both improve performance, while diverse question types and question filtering further benefit adaptation. Case studies indicate that SimRAG generates more relevant, self-contained, and challenging pseudo-labeled question-answer pairs than Llama3-8B-it.

l: SimRAG, SimRAG: Self-Improving Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Adapting Large Language Models to Specialized Domains, Experimental Results / Main Results .. Case Studies
s: SimRAG consistently outperforms baseline models across the medical, scientific, and computer science domains and across multiple question-answering formats. It uses Stage-I retrieval-oriented fine-tuning and Stage-II fine-tuning on self-synthesized training tuples, with average gains over Llama variants of 8.01%, 6.37%, and 8.61% in the three domains, respectively. Its performance is robust to the choice of retriever, and its generated pseudo-labeled data is more relevant, self-contained, and challenging than data generated by the backbone model.

l: Stage-I training, SimRAG: Self-Improving Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Adapting Large Language Models to Specialized Domains, Experimental Results / Main Results .. Case Studies
s: Stage-I performs retrieval-oriented fine-tuning, which significantly improves language-model performance on question-answering tasks compared with the original backbone. After Stage-I, SimRAG generates higher-quality synthetic question-answer pairs, including more self-contained and contextually appropriate examples.

l: Stage-II training, SimRAG: Self-Improving Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Adapting Large Language Models to Specialized Domains, Experimental Results / Main Results .. Case Studies
s: Stage-II fine-tunes language models on self-synthesized training tuples and produces further improvements after Stage-I, with average increases of 2.21% for Llama and 3.50% for Gemma. Including multiple-choice, short-span, and claim-verification data gives the best performance, while removing short-span question answering causes the largest performance drop.

l: retrieval-augmented domain-specific question answering, SimRAG: Self-Improving Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Adapting Large Language Models to Specialized Domains, Experimental Results / Main Results .. Case Studies
s: The unit studies retrieval-augmented question answering in specialized domains and shows that effectively using retrieved context is important for performance. SimRAG is designed to adapt general-domain language models to this setting using unlabeled domain-relevant corpora.

l: domain-specific question answering, SimRAG: Self-Improving Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Adapting Large Language Models to Specialized Domains, Experimental Results / Main Results .. Case Studies
s: The experiments cover domain-specific question answering across 11 datasets in the medical, scientific, and computer science domains. SimRAG improves performance on diverse formats including multiple-choice, assertion, fill-in-the-blank, open-ended generation, short-span question answering, and claim verification.
